To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a hybrid approach combining viscous hydrodynamical evolution of QCD matter with microscopic Boltzmann transport is required to describe the evolution of the fireball produced in ultrareativistic heavy-ion collisions.

the viscous fluid dynamics approach does not provide a quantitative description of hadron gas dynamics, and that the Boltzmann description of the hadron gas is needed to describe the evolution of the system during the hadron gas stage.

1) the viscous fluid dynamics is not able to describe the late stage of the reaction and the hadron resonance chemistry, 2) the extracted values for the effective shear viscosity depend on the hydrodynamic evolution, and hence do not correspond to fundamental transport properties of hadron resonance gases, 3) the hybrid approach provides a more realistic description of the reaction than the viscous hydrodynamical model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the modeling of the space-time dynamics of the fireball in heavy ion collisions.

the development of a hybrid transport approach to describe the expansion of the QCD matter produced by ultrarelativisitc heavy-ion collisions, which is based on the combination of the viscous hydrodynamic description of the dense early stage of the fireball evolution with the microscopic Boltzmann transport approach for the late hadronic stage.
the development of a new hybrid transport approach for viscous QCD dynamics, its implementation in a state-of-the-art event generator and its validation against microscopic transport calculations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
viscous fluid-dynamical models are not able to provide quantitative descriptions of heavy-ion collisions, unless combined with a microscopic transport approach.
the hybrid approach provides a consistent and accurate description of the full time evolution of the fireball from the early deconfined phase to the late dilute hadron resonance gas stage.
the hydrodynamic approach is not able to describe the hadronic phase, but the Boltzmann approach cannot describe the early phase of the reaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hybrid hydrodynamic+Bolzmann approach is a powerful tool for the quantitative description of the bulk evolution of the fireball produced in ultrarelaticivistic heavy-ion reactions.
we developed a new hybrid hydrodynamic+Bolzmann approach and applied it for the bulk evolution and freeze-out of the QCD matter in heavy-ion collisions at LHC energies.

we have developed a novel hybrid approach for the evolution of the fireball and have shown that it is necessary to use both hydrodynamics and a kinetic description to describe the evolution of the hadron gas.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a hybrid approach combining viscous hydrodynamical and microscopic descriptions is a necessary ingredient for a quantitative description and extraction of fundamental transport properties of QCD matter from heavy-ion collision data.

the hydrodynamic evolution of the dense phase of the collision can be used as an effective description of the entire fireball expansion only if the hadronic phase is not treated separately, but rather included in the hydrodynamic evolution.
a realistic description of the hadron gas evolution is needed to extract the transport coefficients of the QCD matter produced at RHIC and the LHC.
